name: 36exp Photographers' School
bioShort: London photographers' school running two-hour evening light-painting workshops at Highgate Tube; open-class, lights supplied.

name: Addy Osmani
bioShort: Long-serving Chrome engineer (Core Web Vitals, Lighthouse, DevTools); now Director at Google Cloud AI covering Gemini, Vertex AI and the Agent Development Kit. Publishes books and essays under his own name.

name: Aidan Gomez
bioShort: British-Canadian co-author of Attention Is All You Need. Cohere is Toronto-headquartered but operates a large London office (Cohere UK Ltd, Companies House 13987418).

name: Aircards
bioShort: WebAR studio, Auggie Award for Most Innovative WebAR App 2023 (Pot Noodle Slurp). No-app-required mobile WebAR across Snap, TikTok, Meta, ARCore, ARKit, visionOS, Unity, Unreal.

name: Alan Jaras
bioShort: St Helens-based retired optical microscopist whose refractograph technique makes lens-less photographs on 35mm film from light refracted through formed glass and plastic.

name: Alex Bradbury
bioShort: Co-founder and CTO of lowRISC; proposed and shipped the upstream RISC-V LLVM backend out of experimental status for LLVM 9.0.

name: Alex Kendall
bioShort: Co-founded Wayve in 2017 out of Cambridge robotics research; pioneered end-to-end deep learning for autonomous driving (AV2.0). OBE 2025; Wayve has raised over $1bn.

name: Ali Dixon
bioShort: Co-founder of XMOS in 2005 (then a Bristol PhD student) alongside James Foster, Noel Hurley, David May and Hitesh Mehta. XMOS xcore processors ship into the AIoT market.

name: All Seeing Eye
bioShort: London immersive studio behind Immersive Histories: Dambusters at the RAF Museum — 1:1 Lancaster reconstruction with VR, haptics, hand-tracking and mocap. Funded through Digital Catapult / CreativeXR.

name: Amit Sood
bioShort: VP and founder of Google Arts & Culture; runs the Paris HQ but commissions across Paris and London sites including UK cultural-tech work.

name: Anagram
bioShort: Pervasive Media Studio residents; Door Into the Dark (Tribeca 2015), The Collider (Sandbox 2019), Goliath (Venice Grand Jury Prize 2021). The most decorated UK non-fiction immersive practice.

name: Andrew Davison
bioShort: Professor of Robot Vision; leads the Dyson Robotics Lab at Imperial. Real-time SLAM, monocular scene mapping, the MASt3R-SLAM line — the reference for spatial intelligence on a single camera.

name: Andrew Lalchan
bioShort: London photographer who documents the Thames-foreshore fire spinning across full moons; sells night-photography prints of the spin work.

name: Andrew Richards
bioShort: Co-founder and CEO of Codeplay Software (Edinburgh) since 2002; chaired the SYCL standards group; Codeplay acquired by Intel in 2022 to anchor oneAPI.

name: Andrew Sloss
bioShort: Co-author of ARM System Developer's Guide (Morgan Kaufmann, 2004); long-serving Arm engineer since 1987. The reference text a generation of ARM systems programmers learned from.

name: Sir Andy Hopper
bioShort: Research Director of Acorn 1979–85 and conceiver of the ARM project; Head of the Cambridge Computer Lab 2004–18; Chair of lowRISC's board. Vice-President of the Royal Society.

name: Anna Barclay
bioShort: Somerset-based festival photographer for Bristol's Circus City; thirteen-year press and editorial track record; the single most comprehensive credited body of UK contemporary-circus performance imagery.

name: Anna Ridler
bioShort: London conceptual artist; Myriad (Tulips) — ten thousand hand-labelled tulip photographs; Mosaic Virus, the GAN piece where bitcoin price drives the bloom. Beazley Design of the Year nominee.

name: Anrick Bregman
bioShort: London-based cross-disciplinary new-realities director: VR, AR, film, games. Director at Unit9, one of London's larger digital production houses.

name: Anthony Geffen
bioShort: CEO of Atlantic Productions; set up Alchemy VR to produce the Attenborough VR titles, including the first BAFTA-winning VR experience. Five-year partnership with the Natural History Museum.

name: Anthony Matchett
bioShort: Co-founded London VR music platform MelodyVR (now LiveOne) in 2015 with Steven Hancock; built the world's largest VR music library with live captures including Disclosure, Kygo, Underworld and the BBC Philharmonic.

name: Apache
bioShort: XR studio based in the St Albans / London orbit; specialises in AR, VR and body-tracking work for brand and broadcast.

name: Arcade XR
bioShort: London-based immersive experience agency; AR storytelling for cultural institutions including the National Gallery, Sky, Disney and UK Parliament.

name: Audiomotion
bioShort: Wheatley, Oxford-based optical mocap house at Rebellion Film Studios; 160 Vicon cameras and one of the largest volumes in the world. Captured the zombies for World War Z, the chariots for Exodus.

name: Ben McOwen Wilson
bioShort: Regional Director for EMEA and Managing Director for the UK & Ireland business at YouTube; long-running public profile through the Royal Television Society.

name: Ben Garfinkel
bioShort: Director of the Centre for the Governance of AI (Oxford); the British centre of gravity for AI-governance research as an academic discipline.

name: Beth Singler
bioShort: British anthropologist of AI and religion; Assistant Professor in Digital Religion(s) at Zurich, previously Junior Research Fellow at Homerton College, Cambridge. Co-editor of The Cambridge Companion to Religion and AI.

name: Bitmap Bureau
bioShort: Southampton-based pixel-art studio (Mike Tucker + Matthew Cope, 2016); ships Xeno Crisis, Battle Axe and Terminator 2D: No Fate on real Mega Drive cartridges.

name: Brave At Night
bioShort: UK studio behind Yes, Your Grace and the curated PixElated Festival pixel-game Steam showcase.

name: Brighton Dome
bioShort: Brighton's Creative Technology programme commissions XR work into the venue itself.

name: Bruce Munro
bioShort: Wiltshire-based British artist with an international large-scale light-installation practice; Field of Light has been re-exhibited at Waddesdon, Salisbury Cathedral and internationally for 25 years.

name: CAMERA — University of Bath
bioShort: Bath research centre with four stages — optical mocap, 4D volumetric, virtual production and face/body light-stage photogrammetry. MyWorld-funded research arm releasing open papers and tooling.

name: Captivate Action
bioShort: Bullards Place E2 mocap training company directed by Lyndall Grant; first to train actors specifically for performance capture in the UK and Australia.

name: Carl Benedikt Frey
bioShort: Dieter Schwarz Associate Professor of AI & Work at the OII; Director of the Future of Work Programme at the Oxford Martin School. Author of The Future of Employment with Michael Osborne.

name: Cassie Kozyrkov
bioShort: Google's first Chief Decision Scientist for almost a decade; left in 2023, now runs the consultancy Kozyr from a public archive of essays on Medium.

name: Catherine Allen
bioShort: BAFTA-winning immersive specialist; led two of the BBC's first VR experiences (2015–16); founded Limina Immersive in 2016 as a VR events / research company that ran the UK's first VR-arts cinema at Watershed Bristol.

name: Cécile Frot-Coutaz
bioShort: Previous YouTube EMEA chief; left in 2021 to become CEO of Sky Studios.

name: Centroid Motion Capture
bioShort: Pinewood-adjacent (now Uxbridge) optical mocap studio; established 1996, 84 Motion Analysis Raptor cameras; Pinewood's preferred mocap supplier with offices at Pinewood and Shepperton.

name: Chocolate Films Workshops
bioShort: UK-wide schools-and-groups light-painting workshops; teaches shutter speed, ISO and aperture through the doing.

name: Chris Benbow
bioShort: Light painter since 2006 publishing as Noctography; writes the standard British tutorial set on EL wire, light stencils, orbs, domes and steel wool.

name: Chris Maltby
bioShort: Rugby, Warwickshire developer; author of GB Studio, the drag-and-drop Game Boy game maker that exports real ROMs and runs on real hardware.

name: Chucklefish
bioShort: London independent developer and publisher founded by Finn Brice in 2011; published Stardew Valley on first release and built the in-house pixel house around Starbound, Wargroove and Witchbrook.

name: Clara Bacou
bioShort: 3D and AR designer/animation director working between London and Los Angeles; Snapchat's inaugural Official Lens Creator; Art Basel Miami Spectacles 3 work with Gucci; joined Meta's Creative Engineering team in 2023 on Orion.

name: Clear Angle Studios
bioShort: UK's lead 3D-capture and processing company; 18 full-body photogrammetry rigs (204 cameras, 32 lights), Dorothy head-scan system, cyberscanning rigs at 200+ DSLRs. Owns DI4D tech and IP since the 2024 acquisition.

name: Coatsink
bioShort: Sunderland-based VR developer founded December 2009; VR titles Shadow Point, Onward, Augmented Empire. Acquired by Thunderful Group in October 2020.

name: Codasip UK
bioShort: European RISC-V processor IP company with strategic UK design centres in Cambridge and Bristol; building the A90 and A110 out-of-order RISC-V cores.

name: Connor Leahy
bioShort: Co-founded Conjecture in London in March 2022 out of EleutherAI; CEO until March 2026; moved to non-profit ControlAI as US Director. Public UK advocate for tight controls on frontier model development.

name: CoSTAR Realtime Lab
bioShort: Abertay-led Dundee virtual-production research lab in partnership with Edinburgh University, CodeBase, Interface and Chroma Developments; £9m investment, hosts a new virtual film academy.

name: CSR (Cambridge Silicon Radio)
bioShort: Bluetooth IP house spun out of Cambridge Consultants in 1998 by Phil O'Donovan, James Collier, Glenn Collinson and others; sold to Qualcomm in 2015 for $2.5bn.

name: Curio
bioShort: Bristol museums and heritage AR sub-brand of Zubr — apps, AR binoculars, interactive trails, 3D scanning. Multiple Sparkies and Museum + Heritage awards.

name: Dame Wendy Hall
bioShort: Regius Professor of Computer Science at Southampton; Executive Director of the Web Science Institute. Co-chaired the UK government's 2017 AI Review.

name: Dan Kunz
bioShort: Flickr handle znuk_d; shot the London Fire Spinners meet from the Thames beach itself — a photographer-in-the-mix frame.

name: Dan Malone
bioShort: Artist behind Speedball 2: Brutal Deluxe and The Chaos Engine; applied to Palace Software in 1985 and went on to EA, Sony and System 3.

name: Dan Whitaker
bioShort: UK long-exposure photographer working with car-trail, star-trail, steel wool and programmable LEDs; early UK member of the Light Painting World Alliance.

name: Daniel Lynch
bioShort: London-based freelance press photographer, BPPA contributor; files for the Express, FT, Independent, Metro and others.

name: David Gilliver
bioShort: Aberdeen-born, Guernsey-based light painter; Glasgow School of Art Fine Art Photography graduate. Long-exposure work, glow stick and orb tool work, self-published e-book and regular workshops.

name: David Krueger
bioShort: Assistant Professor of ML at Cambridge; member of CBL and the Machine Learning Group; research affiliate at CSER and CHAI. Former research director at the UK AI Safety Institute.

name: David May
bioShort: Emeritus Professor of Computer Science at Bristol; lead architect of the Inmos transputer and co-designer of Occam; co-founder and CTO of XMOS in 2005. FRS 1990, FREng 2010.

name: David Silver
bioShort: Led AlphaGo and AlphaZero at DeepMind for 13 years; kept a UCL chair throughout. Left in January 2026 to run Ineffable Intelligence, the RL startup he founded in late 2025.

name: Debbie Weinstein
bioShort: Previously Managing Director of Google UK & Ireland, now President for Europe, Middle East and Africa. Successor to Matt Brittin at the head of Google EMEA.

name: Sir Demis Hassabis
bioShort: Born 1976, London. CEO and co-founder of Google DeepMind and Isomorphic Labs. Nobel Prize in Chemistry 2024 with John Jumper for AlphaFold. Most decorated AI scientist working from Britain.

name: DI4D — Dimensional Imaging
bioShort: Glasgow 4D facial performance capture, founded 2003 by Colin Urquhart; markerless and no-make-up. Credits: Blade Runner 2049, Call of Duty: Modern Warfare trilogy, Black Ops 6, F1. Acquired by Clear Angle Studios.

name: Diana Goss
bioShort: Southsea creative portrait and event photographer (MSc ARPS); teaches night photography and light painting at Portsmouth University and on tour.

name: Digital Catapult
bioShort: UK's industry body for immersive tech; ran the CreativeXR programme with Arts Council England — three cohorts, sixty teams, £851k production funding. Launchpad for No Ghost, All Seeing Eye, Anagram.

name: Dima Damen
bioShort: Professor of Computer Vision at Bristol; leads EPIC-KITCHENS and co-PI on Ego-Exo4D, the joint egocentric-exocentric dataset Meta runs with 13 partner universities. The UK academic Reality Labs Research leans on.

name: Dimension Studio
bioShort: Wimbledon volumetric-capture studio launched by Digital Catapult, Hammerhead and Microsoft Mixed Reality Capture; 106-camera rig; one of three Microsoft-partnered MRC studios in the world.

name: disguise
bioShort: London-headquartered virtual production / extended-reality media-server company. The disguise VX hardware drives LED volumes at MARS, CUBE and many UK virtual-production stages.

name: dock10
bioShort: MediaCityUK, Salford television facility; in 2019 launched a 4K UHD virtual studio using Unreal Engine. Operates the largest virtual studio in the North-West with a Vicon-equipped mocap volume.

name: Drew Henry
bioShort: Founding general manager of Arm's Infrastructure Line of Business 2017–19; guided the launch of Neoverse and established Arm as a serious cloud architecture.

name: DSLR Photography Courses
bioShort: London three-hour intensive on painting with light using LED light gadgets, in the dedicated night-photography programme.

name: East City Films
bioShort: Shoreditch production studio behind Walk to Westerbork, Letters from Drancy and a strand of VR/immersive non-fiction for Channel 4, MTV, Columbia and Sony.

name: Edify
bioShort: Scotland VR education platform developed with Glasgow University; HD learning environments, lesson editor, marketplace and VR-by-proxy mode streaming to Zoom and Teams. £2.5m+ funding since 2017.

name: Edward Grefenstette
bioShort: Former Research Scientist & RL Area Lead, FAIR London until early 2022; honorary professor at UCL DARK; now Head of ML at Cohere. Behind the NetHack and MiniHack lines.

name: Engine Creative
bioShort: Northampton spatial-experiences studio for Barclaycard, BiC, Camelot, Meta and Travis Perkins; in-house REYDAR platform. Credited with the world's first AR magazine and the UK's first AR album cover.

name: EPCC — Mark Parsons
bioShort: Director of EPCC and Dean of Research Computing at Edinburgh; EPCC hosts ARCHER2 (HPE Cray EX, ~28 PFLOP/s, 748,544 AMD EPYC cores), the UK's first National Supercomputing Centre.

name: Epic Games Animation UK
bioShort: Formerly Cubic Motion; Manchester Science Park, Bright Building. Facial animation tech behind God of War, Spider-Man, Hellblade: Senua's Sacrifice. Acquired by Epic in March 2020.

name: Eric Drass
bioShort: Brighton-based; Oxford BSc Philosophy, PhD cognitive psycholinguistics. Works as Shardcore on AI, surveillance and synthetic media. Made the BBC's Ian Hislop deepfake; lectures at the Royal Institution.

name: EuphoriaXR
bioShort: Watford-based WebAR, WebVR, AI-driven XR app and enterprise training simulation studio shipping across UK and US markets; founded 2016.

name: Factory 42
bioShort: London immersive studio behind Hold the World with David Attenborough (D&AD award) at the Natural History Museum, and the Green Planet AR experience.

name: Faceware Technologies
bioShort: Spin-off from Image Metrics (out of the University of Manchester); US-headquartered now, UK roots. Trusted by Rockstar, Ubisoft, ILM — the head-mounted camera most often seen on UK performers.

name: FreeMoCap
bioShort: Open-source markerless mocap system using multiple webcams and MediaPipe-class pose networks. Research-grade output for the price of cameras; active Discord and GitHub.

name: Freya Murray
bioShort: Creative-lead role at Google Arts & Culture Lab in London; commissioned MLF's Nest with Erland Cooper and Es Devlin's A National Portrait at the NPG.

name: Future Visual
bioShort: Brighton-based VISIONxR platform for enterprise VR training and collaboration; works heavily in aviation and behaviour-change training, founded 2015.

name: Gary J. Lucken
bioShort: Bournemouth-based (London-born) British pixel artist; most widely published practitioner working today. Clients include BBC, Honda, Sony, The Guardian and Nestlé.

name: Gim Liu
bioShort: UK & Hong Kong commercial photographer and long-exposure specialist; author of A Beginner's Guide to After Dark Photography with Gimagery (2022). The maximalist's textbook for the UK.

name: Goldsmiths EAVI
bioShort: Embodied AudioVisual Interaction lab at Goldsmiths, New Cross; mocap sits next to eye-tracking, BCI and physiological bio-interfaces. Dr Dan Strutt's work on digital dance aesthetic; open-source Goldsmiths Mocap Streamer (AHRC).

name: Goldsmiths VR Lab
bioShort: Ben Pimlott Building; multi-camera mocap stage, 8.1 Ambisonic surround, custom Oculus Rift / Leap Motion rigs. Hosts the MA/MSc Virtual and Augmented Reality.

name: Graphcore
bioShort: Bristol AI silicon company building the Intelligence Processing Unit on the bet that AI workloads are graph workloads. Acquired by SoftBank in July 2024 for around $500m.

name: Gravity Sketch
bioShort: Royal College of Art spinout founded 2014 by Guillaume Couche, Pierre Paslier, Oluwaseyi Sosanya and Daniela Paredes Fuentes; cross-platform 3D modelling for designers used by Ford, Nissan, Reebok and 60+ universities.

name: Heinrich Küttler
bioShort: Engineer behind the NetHack Learning Environment, the procedurally-generated RL benchmark at FAIR London; based at FAIR's King's Cross office.

name: Helen Kelisky
bioShort: Managing Director of Google Cloud UK & Ireland; arrived in 2022 after 30 years across IBM, Salesforce and OpenText.

name: Helen Margetts
bioShort: Professor of Society and the Internet at the Oxford Internet Institute; Programme Director for Public Policy at the Alan Turing Institute. OBE.

name: Henk Nieborg
bioShort: Gelselaar, Netherlands; art director at UK studio Bitmap Bureau. Pushes pixels since 1985; credits include Shantae, Contra 4 and Bitmap Bureau's Mega Drive titles.

name: Henry Shevlin
bioShort: Joined DeepMind in May 2026 in the Philosopher role for machine consciousness; splits time with Cambridge as Associate Director of the Leverhulme Centre for the Future of Intelligence.

name: Henry Stuart
bioShort: Founded Fitzrovia VR/AR/360 agency Visualise in 2011; 60+ VR experiences for BBC, Audi, Wimbledon, Economist, MSF, Samsung, O2. Speaking on VR production internationally since 2006.

name: Hermann Hauser
bioShort: Co-founder of Acorn Computers in 1978; author of the ARM spinout decision in 1990; later founder of Amadeus Capital Partners. KBE, FRS.

name: Holdens
bioShort: Longest-running Manchester AR shop — the first agency in the city to ship AR commercially in 2016. Marketing-led with a consistent Manchester presence.

name: Holition
bioShort: Holborn Circus retail and beauty AR specialist; Charlotte Tilbury's magic mirror try-on, Burberry Virtual Studio, Jo Malone Virtual Townhouse, work for LVMH, Hermès, Coty, Estée Lauder and PUIG.

name: Holly Herndon & Mat Dryhurst
bioShort: Berlin-based but Dryhurst is UK-born; major 2024 work The Call was made with 15 UK community choirs for the Serpentine. Co-founded Spawning in 2022; the Holly+ AI voice clone (2021) is the canonical artist-led consent example.

name: Humanloop
bioShort: London LLM evaluation platform; UCL spin-out co-founded in 2020 by Raza Habib (UCL ML PhD), Peter Hayes and Jordan Burgess.

name: Iain Murray
bioShort: Professor of Machine Learning and Inference at the School of Informatics, Edinburgh; PhD from UCL under Zoubin Ghahramani; Fellow of the ELLIS Unit Edinburgh.

name: Ian Hobson
bioShort: Tyneside veteran light painter publishing as lightpainting.org.uk since the analogue era; ex-neuropharmacology. Works straight out of camera with torch, EL wire, Pixelstick and improvised tools.

name: Ian Hogarth
bioShort: Chair of the UK Government's AI Safety Institute from June 2023, remained Chair when renamed AI Security Institute in February 2025. Co-author of the annual State of AI Report.

name: Iason Gabriel
bioShort: Senior Staff Research Scientist at DeepMind; teaches moral and political philosophy at Oxford; runs the AGI & Society team. His paper on AI value alignment is the standard reference.

name: Imageplotter (Chris)
bioShort: Alamy Live News stringer shooting the LFS beach using in-camera multiple exposures, plus protest and gig coverage across central London.

name: Imaginarium Studios
bioShort: Founded 2011 by Andy Serkis and Jonathan Cavendish; at Pinewood and Tileyard in King's Cross with SIDE. Star Wars work, The Tempest with the RSC, Amazon's The Girlfriend.

name: Imagination Technologies
bioShort: Kings Langley, Hertfordshire — PowerVR GPU IP house. Tile-based deferred rendering powered every iPhone GPU through to 2017; recent Catapult RISC-V CPU line.

name: Imitating the Dog
bioShort: Leeds-based 20-year practice fusing live performance with digital and mixed-reality technology; Frankenstein, Dracula: The Untold Story, Night of the Living Dead — Remix with Leeds Playhouse.

name: Imperial College Computer Vision
bioShort: Real-time scene understanding lab for robotics, self-driving and AR/VR — the underpinning machine vision that lets AR experiences register to the world geometrically.

name: Immerse UK
bioShort: National network for the UK immersive industries; chaired in recent years by Sol Rogers. The grant/policy-facing organisation tying the regions together.

name: Jabir Grant
bioShort: Scotland-based sprite animator on Final Vendetta at Bitmap Bureau; spent more than two years drawing every sprite animation in the game.

name: Jake Elwes
bioShort: British media artist; AI, queer theory and technical bias. Zizi — Queering the Dataset (2019) and The Zizi Show, a deepfake drag cabaret; the ongoing Zizi Project intervenes in face-recognition training data.

name: James Bridle
bioShort: British writer and artist born 1980; author of New Dark Age (Verso 2018) and Ways of Being (2022). Hosted BBC Radio 4's New Ways of Seeing.

name: Jem Davies
bioShort: 18 years at Arm, latterly Arm Fellow and VP of Technology in the Media Processing Division; set the Mali GPU and video roadmap; founding GM of Arm's Machine Learning Group.

name: Jon Davies
bioShort: UK freelance pixel artist with nearly twenty years in the industry; credits include Super House of Dead Ninjas, Binding of Isaac, Inmost, Cursed to Golf, X-Men '97 and Marvel: Cosmic Invasion.

name: JonThePhotographer
bioShort: London-based DSLR + flow-arts photographer; a regular at the OXO Tower foreshore London Fire Spinners meet, Leake Street, and the wider walls / tunnel / foreshore circuit.

name: Jonathan Pow
bioShort: Harrogate-based editorial photographer; his Samhuinn Fire Festival gallery on PhotoShelter is one of the better single-night documentations of the Calton Hill work.

name: Joseph Yiu
bioShort: Distinguished Engineer, system architecture, Arm. Joined 2001; works on Cortex-M processor and design-kit projects; wrote the definitive reference guides to Cortex-M0, M3 and M4.

name: Junyoung Chung
bioShort: DeepMind reinforcement-learning researcher; AlphaStar, AlphaCode, Veo.

name: Karén Simonyan
bioShort: VGGNet co-author (with Andrew Zisserman, Oxford); Principal Research Scientist at DeepMind 2014; role in AlphaZero, AlphaFold, WaveNet, BigGAN, Flamingo. Co-founded Inflection AI; Chief Scientist at Microsoft AI from March 2024.

name: Kitt Bunney
bioShort: Credited official photographer for the Beltane Fire Society's festivals (Beltane in April/May, Samhuinn at Hallowe'en).

name: Koray Kavukcuoglu
bioShort: CTO of Google DeepMind and Chief AI Architect at Google; led the teams behind DQN, IMPALA and WaveNet.

name: Krste Asanović
bioShort: Co-founder and Chief Architect of SiFive; Chief Architect of RISC-V International; Professor Emeritus at UC Berkeley. Cambridge-educated; SiFive opened a Cambridge office in 2022.

name: LAMDA — Motion Capture
bioShort: 30-camera MOCAP studio at the academy and a two-day artist-led course aimed at actors with no prior mocap.

name: lay3d
bioShort: Edinburgh independent AR and VR development studio.

name: LED Eddie
bioShort: Woking-based long-running British torchlight and rotating-rig practitioner active on Flickr since 2009; camera-rotation technique cited as a teaching reference.

name: Libby Heaney
bioShort: British artist and quantum physicist; Imperial physics first 2005; PhD on mode entanglement; the first artist to use quantum computing as a working medium. Lumen Prize Immersive Environment 2022.

name: Lila Ibrahim
bioShort: Built DeepMind from a research lab to a 2,500-person organisation; came in 2018 from Coursera, after Kleiner Perkins, after 18 years at Intel. Now Chief AI Readiness Officer.

name: lowRISC — Robert Mullins
bioShort: Robert Mullins — Professor of Computer Architecture at Cambridge; co-founder and director of lowRISC, co-founder of the Raspberry Pi Foundation. lowRISC stewards OpenTitan and the Ibex 32-bit RISC-V core.

name: Manchester Metropolitan — Creative AR/VR Hub
bioShort: MMU business-school's commercial AR/VR research hub — who pays, how scale happens, what the commercial AR/VR sector looks like as it grows.

name: Marco Gillies
bioShort: Professor in the Department of Computing at Goldsmiths; interactive machine learning for embodied interaction design (with Rebecca Fiebrink at UAL CCI).

name: Mariana Mazzucato
bioShort: Professor in the Economics of Innovation and Public Value at UCL; founding Director of UCL IIPP. Author of The Entrepreneurial State, The Value of Everything, Mission Economy.

name: Mark Boot
bioShort: London-born (1965); lectures at De Montfort University since 2001. Sculptor first and photographer second; works EL wire and LEDs into expanded-polystyrene forms.

name: Marshmallow Laser Feast
publicBrand: Robin McNicholas, Barney Steel, Ersin Han Ersin
bioShort: Hackney Wick experiential art collective founded 2011; In the Eyes of the Animal, EVOLVER (Cannes Immersive 2024), Of the Oak at Kew. The most internationally exhibited London VR-art studio.

name: Marta Krupinska
bioShort: Ran Google Campus London after Eze Vidra until its 2021 closure; co-founded CUR8 and chairs startup boards.

name: Mati Staniszewski & Piotr Dąbkowski
bioShort: Co-founded ElevenLabs in 2022; UK Eleven Labs Ltd registered at 33 Broadwick Street, declared worldwide HQ in 2024. Voice cloning and AI dubbing at scale. Staniszewski named to TIME's 100 most influential people in AI 2025.

name: Matt Brittin
bioShort: Ran Google EMEA business and operations until early 2025; in May 2026 announced as the next BBC Director-General.

name: Matthew Applegate
bioShort: Suffolk chiptune composer and educator treating the Game Boy and Speak & Spell as instruments; performed at BBC Maida Vale, Bletchley Park and the National Museum of Computing. BAFTA YGD Mentor Award 2019.

name: Maze Theory
bioShort: London VR game developer founded 2018; Doctor Who: The Edge of Time, Peaky Blinders: The King's Ransom. The closest UK studio to AAA-licensed VR storytelling.

name: MediaCity Immersive Technologies Innovation Hub
bioShort: Salford Quays convening body for North-West immersive tech — virtual production, AI, AR/VR and game-engine work; where Manchester/Salford XR companies connect with industry partners.

name: Mel Slater
bioShort: Founded the VECG group at UCL; EPSRC Senior Research Fellow since 1999. The UK's most cited VR-presence researcher; also ICREA Research Professor at Universitat de Barcelona leading the Event Lab.

name: Memo Akten
bioShort: Istanbul-born London-based multidisciplinary artist; Goldsmiths PhD under Mick Grierson and Rebecca Fiebrink. Prix Ars Electronica Golden Nica. Learning to See is a founding work of contemporary AI art.

name: Meta AI research index
bioShort: Meta's publicly-listed canon of FAIR work; the corporate counterpart to the named UK FAIR London researchers' personal sites.

name: Michael Bosanko
bioShort: Cardiff light painter and photographer over a decade in; no compositing — portraiture, landscape and commercial. Writes for the digital-camera press.

name: Mick Grierson
bioShort: Professor and Research Leader at UAL CCI, which he co-founded in 2018 after a decade developing Creative Computing at Goldsmiths. Signal processing, ML and information retrieval for creative practice.

name: Mick Stephenson
bioShort: UK self-taught ex-builder, now full-time light artist; won Lumiere's BRILLIANT prize in 2011. Best known for the Litre of Light projects: recycled plastic bottles lit with LEDs at Durham, London, Cambridge and beyond.

name: Mike Muller
bioShort: Co-founder of Arm; CTO 1990–2019; ran hardware strategy and portable products at Acorn before the spinout.

name: Mike Tucker
bioShort: Southampton co-founder of Bitmap Bureau (with Matthew Cope) in 2016; background at IOMO and Megadev before pivoting the studio toward 2D pixel work on retro hardware.

name: Mikayel Samvelyan
bioShort: Worked in FAIR London's open-endedness team 2020–2024 while completing UCL PhD under Tim Rocktäschel; contributed to Llama 3 safety work (Rainbow Teaming). Now at DeepMind.

name: Misha Denil
bioShort: Spent a decade at DeepMind on language models; keeps mdenil.com as the public bibliography.

name: Mo-Sys Engineering
bioShort: Greenwich camera tracking and virtual-production technology; converting an old Greenwich power station into an eight-stage virtual production hub. Mo-Sys StarTracker is a European LED-volume standard.

name: The Mocap Studio
bioShort: London volume that publishes its rates and aims itself at animation, VFX and VR clients who do not need the Pinewood scale.

name: The Mocap Vaults
bioShort: London + LA industry-veteran-run actor workshops on a professional stage; SummitUK event puts performers in suit for two days with HD scene footage for showreel.

name: Mode 7 Games
bioShort: Oxford studio of Paul Kilduff-Taylor and Ian Hardingham; best known for Frozen Synapse and for publishing Tokyo 42 by SMAC Games.

name: Move AI
bioShort: UK markerless pioneer since 2019. Genesis flagship post-process; Move Live runs at under 100ms latency in 10m x 10m space. Clients include EA, Nike, Ubisoft. Disguise partnership puts the tech inside virtual-production LED stages.

name: Murray Shanahan
bioShort: Professor of Cognitive Robotics at Imperial; Principal Scientist at DeepMind since 2017. Scientific advisor to Ex Machina; his book Embodiment and the Inner Life seeded the screenplay.

name: Mustafa Suleyman
bioShort: Co-founded DeepMind in 2010; headed applied AI; left in 2022 to co-found Inflection AI with Reid Hoffman and Karen Simonyan; joined Microsoft in March 2024 as EVP and CEO of Microsoft AI. CBE. Author of The Coming Wave.

name: Magpie Photography
bioShort: Manchester creative and documentary photographer; blog includes circus and parade documentation tied to Manchester Day and other public events.

name: NCCA — Bournemouth University
bioShort: National Centre for Computer Animation, established 1989. Research across computer animation, 3D intelligent virtual humans, computer vision, gaming, immersive tech, physics-based simulation and digital twins. AccessMocap is the NCCA's in-house service.

name: nDreams
bioShort: Farnborough VR game developer founded 2006; now the largest pure-play VR game developer in the world. Acquired by Aonic for $110m in November 2023.

name: Neel Nanda
bioShort: Cambridge maths 2020; Mechanistic Interpretability Team Lead at Google DeepMind; creator of TransformerLens; public face of mechanistic interpretability through YouTube walkthroughs.

name: Neon8
bioShort: Scotland-based independent VR production studio.

name: Nexus Studios
bioShort: Academy Award-nominated animation house turned AR/VR studio; long collaboration with Google Spotlight Stories — Back to the Moon (Emmy-nominated), Rain or Shine. Founded 2000.

name: Niantic — London
bioShort: London office and research lab seeded by the 2018 acquisition of Matrix Mill (UCL CV spin-out); carries Niantic's AR Cloud / Lightship work. Acquired 8th Wall in 2022 and open-sourced it under MIT in early 2026.

name: Nicholas Goodden
bioShort: London urban photographer working across street, graffiti and commercial; early UK Pixelstick adopter in 2013. Commissioned work for Citroën, Beavertown and Peugeot.

name: Nigel Stephens
bioShort: Lead ISA Architect and Arm Fellow; first author on the 2018 paper documenting the Scalable Vector Extension; ran the multi-year SVE project across Arm Research and Architecture and Technology.

name: Nigel Topham
bioShort: Professor at Edinburgh Informatics; Director of the Institute for Computing Systems Architecture; led the ARC-600 at ARC International and the EnCore research processor at Edinburgh.

name: Sir Nigel Shadbolt
bioShort: Principal of Jesus College, Oxford; Professorial Research Fellow in Oxford CS; Chairman of the Open Data Institute, which he co-founded with Tim Berners-Lee.

name: No Ghost
bioShort: East London Emmy-winning immersive content studio (founded 2015); made Madrid Noir (Children & Family Emmy) and Wallace & Gromit: The Grand Getaway with Aardman and Atlas V on Meta Quest.

name: Nikola Mrkšić
bioShort: London — Cambridge PhD; first hire at VocalIQ (the Cambridge ML spin-out Apple bought in 2015 and folded into Siri). Co-founded PolyAI in 2017 with Tsung-Hsien Wen and Pei-Hao Su.

name: NOVAK
bioShort: Newcastle upon Tyne award-winning creative studio in projection mapping and motion design; their 195 Piccadilly piece for Lumiere London 2016 used the BAFTA archive. Regulars at Lumiere Durham, London, Derry, Edinburgh and Leeds.

name: Oriol Vinyals
bioShort: VP of Research and a tech lead on Gemini; co-author of the original seq2seq paper and the AlphaStar lead.

name: Patrick Lewis
bioShort: First-author on the original RAG paper (2020); PhD split between FAIR London and UCL under Sebastian Riedel and Pontus Stenetorp. Now at Cohere leading RAG, tool-use and agents.

name: Paul Atherton Photography
bioShort: Manchester event photographer covering Salford and the city centre with entertainment and cultural events in portfolio.

name: Paul Calleja
bioShort: Director of Cambridge Research Computing Services and the Cambridge Open Zettascale Lab; oversaw the Dawn AI supercomputer (Intel Xeon + Data Center GPU Max) at West Cambridge.

name: Pebble Studios
bioShort: Shoreditch studio, one of the UK's first dedicated VR studios; ports the same craft sensibility to AR filters and mobile experiences for Adidas, Samsung, L'Oreal and Live Nation.

name: Penelope Barritt
bioShort: Editorial and stock photographer; documents the London Fire Spinners' monthly full-moon meet on the OXO Tower foreshore.

name: perkster
bioShort: Flickr handle; Thames foreshore fire spinners in long-exposure panorama (Fuji X-T2, 30-second exposure).

name: Pervasive Media Studio
bioShort: Bristol research studio at the Watershed; partnership between Watershed, UWE Bristol and the University of Bristol. ~200 artists, technologists and academics. Home of the Bristol VR Lab.

name: Peter Greenhalgh
bioShort: Lead architect of Cortex-A7 and Cortex-A53; led the development of big.LITTLE; now SVP Technology and Fellow at Arm. Holds 20 CPU microarchitecture patents.

name: Phill Fisher
bioShort: Devizes, Wiltshire-based light painter; works in-camera with no editing; photographs ruins, memorials and statues at night, expanded into drone-mounted light painting.

name: Photoion School of Photography
bioShort: London night-photography workshop using Golden Jubilee Bridge and Westminster; includes painting-with-light segments.

name: The Photography Project
bioShort: Bristol Harbourside low-light and night-photography workshops: traffic-light trails, painting with light, long-exposure colour.

name: Pixel Artworks
bioShort: London immersive experience design and production studio; installation portfolio uses LED, projection and pixel-mapped surfaces across retail and museum work.

name: Pixel Pusher Games
bioShort: UK studio building homebrew titles for real Mega Drive cartridges: a post-cyberpunk visual novel (Chords) and a first-person horror adventure (Crypt of Dracula).

name: Pixomondo London
bioShort: London virtual production studio with an LED volume (opened September 2021). Pixomondo runs the LED volume that shot The Mandalorian; London joined a network across Frankfurt, Stuttgart, LA, Toronto and Montreal.

name: PRELOADED
bioShort: London BAFTA-winning immersive games studio founded 2000; Phil Stuart is co-founder and ECD. Clients include McDonald's, LEGO, the BBC; partners include Niantic, Magic Leap, HTC and Google. Now part of Learning Technologies Group.

name: Prem Akkaraju
bioShort: Former CEO of Weta Digital; appointed CEO of Stability AI on 25 June 2024 as part of the Sean Parker-led rescue. Stability is the British company behind Stable Diffusion.

name: Pushmeet Kohli
bioShort: VP of Research at Google DeepMind, leading the AI for Science and Strategic Initiatives Unit; founder of the team behind Isomorphic Labs and a co-author on AlphaFold. Partners with the UK AI Security Institute.

name: Rachel Cunningham
bioShort: Little Clacton, Essex pixel artist whose visible discipline is the demake — taking modern games and reimagining them in 8-bit / 16-bit fixed-palette keys.

name: RADiCAL
bioShort: Single-camera real-time markerless mocap from webcam or phone; core tech acquired by Autodesk in 2026 — heavy presence in the UK indie animation pipeline.

name: Raia Hadsell
bioShort: VP of Research at DeepMind; runs the Frontier AI unit. Founded TMLR as an open-access alternative to NeurIPS-cycle publishing.

name: Raindance Immersive
bioShort: London indie-leaning immersive festival curated by María Rakušanová; runs both as a physical London event and a month-long social-VR festival on VRChat and Resonite.

name: Recode XR Studio
bioShort: Manchester XR and virtual-production studio — LED volume plus AI-driven workflows for film, TV, commercials and branded content.

name: Red Wren Studios
bioShort: Ipswich, Suffolk event and wedding photographer who has done dedicated fire-performer shoots with Penny Pyro and Farren (fire breathing).

name: Reflex Arc
bioShort: Three-time BAFTA-nominated XR and spatial-computing studio; long-running digital partner of David Hockney plus immersive work for Sky, HSBC and cultural institutions. Founded 2011.

name: Rene Haas
bioShort: CEO of Arm since February 2022; joined Arm in October 2013 after seven years at Nvidia; was Arm's CCO and President of IP Products Group before becoming CEO. Took the company public on Nasdaq in 2023.

name: Reuben Wu
bioShort: Liverpool-born (1975), Sheffield Hallam industrial-design graduate, founder member of Ladytron; now based in Chicago. Came on drone-LED light painting in 2015; built Lux Noctis and Light Storm series. National Geographic photographer since 2022.

name: REWIND
bioShort: Founded 2011 as a VFX house, pivoted to immersive; clients include HBO, Paramount, BBC, NBC, Nike, Sony, Björk, Rolls-Royce. Sol Rogers chairs Immerse UK and sits on the BAFTA VR Advisory Group.

name: Richard Grisenthwaite
bioShort: EVP, Chief Architect and Fellow at Arm; led the long-term architecture from Armv6 onwards; shipped TrustZone, multiprocessor extensions, virtualisation; partnered with Fujitsu on SVE for Fugaku.

name: Richard Newcombe
bioShort: VP of Research Science, Reality Labs Research; runs the research-science side of Reality Labs and is the most-cited engineering author on Project Aria. US-based but the node UK academic partners route through.

name: Rigu
bioShort: UK stockist for Light Painting Brushes — the supplier the British fibre-optic-brush practice flows through.

name: Robert Kirk
bioShort: Former PhD student at UCL DARK (FAIR-adjacent); wrote the canonical survey of generalisation in deep RL under Tim Rocktäschel and Edward Grefenstette. Now research scientist at the UK AI Security Institute.

name: Roberta Raileanu
bioShort: Started and led the Tool Use team for Llama 3 while at FAIR London; now at Google DeepMind and honorary lecturer at UCL.

name: Sir Robin Saxby
bioShort: Arm's first CEO 1991–2001; the architect of the IP-licensing model that gave Arm its 95% share of the mobile-phone CPU market. FRS, FREng, knighted 2002.

name: Rosetta Whitehead
bioShort: Brighton long-exposure light painter with a background in holography; surreal in-camera imagery without Photoshop.

name: Ross Ashton
bioShort: Creative director of The Projection Studio (founded 2010); trained in France in son et lumière before bringing architectural mapping into the British public-realm canon. AV Professional of the Year 2019. Guinness World Record holder for Face Britain.

name: Ross Jukes
bioShort: Birmingham photographer and videographer; long-running wire-wool / steel-wool series shot around Birmingham's canals.

name: Royal Shakespeare Company — The Tempest
bioShort: November 2016 Stratford-then-London Tempest; Mark Quartley performed Ariel live in a 17-sensor suit driving a projected avatar in real time. First major stage production with live mocap.

name: Royal College of Art — InnovationRCA
bioShort: The MA that produced Gravity Sketch; InnovationRCA incubates VR/XR product spinouts.

name: Royal Central School of Speech & Drama — PTEQ
bioShort: Swiss Cottage Centre for Performance Technology and Equity; runs the only dedicated MOCAP-showreel service for UK actors plus the two-day Introduction to Motion Capture for Performance.

name: Sam Dutton
bioShort: Long-serving Developer Advocate for Chrome; lived in London since 1986; maintains github.com/samdutton plus the WebRTC sample library at simpl.info.

name: Sam Dyer
bioShort: Founded the Bristol independent publishing house in 2014; catalogue runs to ~40 thread-sewn titles covering NES, SNES, Commodore 64, Master System, GBA. Treats pixel art as a design field in its own right.

name: Scenegraph Studios
bioShort: Greater Manchester XR-as-a-Service studio working across Unreal, Omniverse, cloud rendering, AI and mocap. Built Spirit VR for mental-wellbeing applications; also Fortnite-universe builds.

name: Sean J Connolly
bioShort: Richmond, North Yorkshire fashion, lifestyle and event photographer who publishes steel-wool tutorials and shoot writeups.

name: Sean Rodrigo
bioShort: London-based VR painter; works under Continuum VR doing live painting, training, storyboards, previs and concept art directly inside VR. Commissioned work for Digital Catapult, Framestore, Mercedes, Adobe, Barclays Eagle Labs.

name: Sebastian Riedel
bioShort: Former Research Scientist, FAIR London; held the longest-running joint chair between FAIR London and UCL, supervising a generation of PhD students. The retrieval line of work (including the original RAG paper) began with his students.

name: Sébastien Lemaire
bioShort: Third of the Beltane Fire Society's credited photographers, spanning both Beltane and Samhuinn festivals.

name: SENSEcity
bioShort: Brighton AR-specific studio tied to the FutureScope Heritage XR programme at the Grade I-listed Corn Exchange.

name: Shahwali Shayan
bioShort: Runs Shahnanigans studio out of London and lectures at the Royal College of Art; AR campaigns for Samsung, Disney, Netflix, Adobe, Hugo Boss, Sony Music. GhostsOfThePast installation around Tate Modern was his RCA graduation project.

name: Shane Legg
bioShort: Co-founder of DeepMind; now Chief AGI Scientist at Google DeepMind leading the Technical AGI Safety team. PhD from IDSIA under Marcus Hutter on machine super-intelligence (AIXI). CBE 2019.

name: The Sharp Project
bioShort: 200,000 sq ft converted Sharp warehouse opened 2011, hosting creative digital businesses and green-screen production. The building several Manchester AR studios rent space inside.

name: Silverchip
bioShort: Manchester AR/VR development house with a healthcare-VR specialism; long-running clinical and training builds for NHS partners.

name: Simon Beresford-Wylie
bioShort: CEO of Imagination Technologies through the Chinese-ownership period; announced 2025 retirement.

name: Simon Fenney
bioShort: One of the original architects of the 1992 Trident Project at what became Imagination; the route into tile-based deferred rendering that has powered every PowerVR generation and every iPhone GPU through 2017.

name: Simon Knowles
bioShort: Co-founder and CTO of Graphcore in Bristol; previously co-founder of Icera (sold to Nvidia for $367M). The architectural choice to build for graphs rather than tensors is his signature.

name: Simon Segars
bioShort: Joined Arm in 1991 as the 16th employee; led ARM7 and ARM9 cores that powered the first digital mobile phones; CEO July 2013–February 2022. Steered the SoftBank acquisition in 2016. FRS 2024.

name: Sliced Bread Animation
bioShort: London VR/AR/animation studio; marketing and corporate VR work with a strong publishing thread on VR-pipeline practicalities. Candid Develop:Brighton talks on production realities.

name: Sola (Peter Medlicott)
bioShort: Birmingham; working as Sola since 2006 and credited as the pioneer of landscape light graffiti. Uses EL wire alongside torches and handheld LEDs, straight out of camera.

name: Sophie Wilson
bioShort: Co-designed the original ARM ISA in 1983; author of BBC BASIC; later Chief Architect of Broadcom's Firepath. Fellow of the Royal Society, CBE. Over 230 billion ARM cores shipped since 1985.

name: Soumith Chintala
bioShort: Co-creator of PyTorch and lead core maintainer until 2025; stepped back from both PyTorch leadership and Meta in November 2025 after 11 years. The PyTorch UK ecosystem was shaped by his tenure.

name: spark-ar-creators (Edoardo Tosti)
bioShort: Community-maintained registry of Spark AR creators with over 9,000 entries — not a Meta property but the only public, queryable trace of who was building on the platform when it shut.

name: SpiNNaker research group
bioShort: Manchester academic end of the Arm diaspora: a million Arm cores wired into a custom packet-switched fabric to simulate spiking neural networks at biological rates.

name: Stephen Cave
bioShort: Academic Director of the Leverhulme Centre for the Future of Intelligence; Co-Director of the Institute for Technology and Humanity at Cambridge. Co-editor of AI Narratives, Imagining AI and Feminist AI (OUP).

name: Steve Furber
bioShort: Principal designer of the BBC Micro and the first ARM processor at Acorn; ICL Professor (Emeritus) at Manchester where he leads SpiNNaker — a million ARM cores in parallel modelling the human brain. CBE, FRS, FREng.

name: StoryFutures & StoryFutures Academy
bioShort: Run by Royal Holloway with the NFTS; the UK's National Centre for Immersive Storytelling. Mentoring scheme run by ILM Immersive; 40+ R&D collaborations, 16 new products, 100+ companies in network.

name: Studio Wayne McGregor
bioShort: Choreographer's lab founded 1992; real-time mocap in +/-Human alongside Random International's drone flock; ABBA Voyage capture sessions; resident choreographer at the Royal Ballet.

name: StudioT3D
bioShort: London and Gateshead mocap volume plus virtual-production stage run by Target3D — the UK's sole OptiTrack distributor and the hardware integrator behind a large fraction of the country's mocap installs.

name: Sue Black
bioShort: Professor of Computer Science and Technology Evangelist at Durham. Research on algorithmic bias and software fairness; founded BCSWomen in 1998; led the Bletchley Park save campaign; runs #TechUPWomen. OBE.

name: Sumo Digital
bioShort: Sheffield-based studio founded 2003; acquired CCP Newcastle's VR studio in January 2018, folding VR work into a wider AAA pipeline.

name: Surround Vision
bioShort: The Old Truman Brewery, Brick Lane E1; 10+ years of 360 / VR production. Built the piggy-back carbon 360 rig used by Sky Sports OB; volumetric, live VR, sports, fashion, culture.

name: Victor Riparbelli
bioShort: Co-founded Synthesia in 2017 with Matthias Nießner, Lourdes Agapito and Steffen Tjerrild; Britain's largest generative-AI firm by revenue. Raised Series E in October 2025 at a $4bn valuation.

name: Target3D
bioShort: UK's sole OptiTrack distributor; supports, integrates and rents inertial mocap; the studio behind a large fraction of UK location-mocap shoots, even when uncredited.

name: The Captury
bioShort: Multi-camera markerless mocap distributed in the UK by Target3D; used for sports biomechanics and clinical-gait work as much as for entertainment.

name: THINKlab — University of Salford
bioShort: Part of the School of Science, Engineering & Environment at Salford; VR research across resilient cities, smart cities, collaborative engineering and virtual training. Built Virtual Chernobyl, RHS Bridgewater VR, Design4Energy.

name: Tim Gamble
bioShort: Manchester award-winning long-exposure light artist since 2013; UK brand ambassador for Light Painting Brushes. Produces complex worlds in a kitchen-table-sized footprint, 99% in-camera.

name: Tim Jackson
bioShort: Southampton-based landscape and astrophotography photographer running a steel-wool spinning series.

name: Tim Rocktäschel
bioShort: Former Manager & Research Scientist at FAIR London, ran the open-ended-learning programme through 2023. Professor of AI at UCL DARK; after FAIR became Director and Principal Scientist at Google DeepMind. Founding new venture Recursive Superintelligence in 2026.

name: Tom Schaul
bioShort: Reinforcement-learning researcher; prioritised experience replay, intrinsic motivation.

name: Tony Sellen
bioShort: London long-exposure photographer; his Long Exposure London series is a baseline reference for night-photography in the capital.

name: Tudor Brown
bioShort: Co-founder of Arm; Principal Engineer at founding, CTO then COO then President 2008–12. MBE, FREng. Cambridge Electrical Sciences.

name: The Alan Turing Institute
bioShort: UK's independent national institute for data science and AI, based at the British Library, London. George Williamson incoming Chief Executive from May 2026; Jean Innes 2023–2025; Adrian Smith 2018–2023.

name: UCL Immersive Virtual Environments Laboratory
bioShort: Inside the VECG group in UCL Computer Science; VR, AR, MR, smart geometry processing, digital reality, graphics and illumination, sensors and systems. The Matrix Mill spin-out came from this lineage.

name: University of Portsmouth — CCIXR
bioShort: Centre for Creative and Immersive Extended Reality; 48 Vicon Vantage cameras plus 40-camera Vicon Origin active system. Alumni go to Rockstar, Vicon, Imaginarium and Weta.

name: University of Salford — DipHE Motion Capture
bioShort: UK's first dedicated diploma in motion capture technology; two-year course built with Cloud Imperium and dock10.

name: Vicky Hellfire (Vic Pannett)
bioShort: London/Essex fire and glow performer, photographer and stilt walker; rare working fire performer who also runs a photography practice.

name: Vicon
bioShort: Yarnton, Oxfordshire; spun out of Oxford Medical Systems in 1984; the Valkyrie cameras are the current flagship. The cameras hanging on most ceilings in UK mocap.

name: Vidushi Marda
bioShort: Human-rights lawyer with a UK research base; Director of Ecosystem Building at the AI Collaborative; co-founded REAL ML. Cited by the Indian Supreme Court and the House of Lords AI Select Committee.

name: Visualise
bioShort: London XR agency in the Biscuit Factory, Bermondsey; VR + AR + 360 + volumetric and large-scale installation work since 2011. Louis Vuitton AR work for the Vendôme maison facade.

name: Volodymyr Mnih
bioShort: Reinforcement-learning researcher; the DQN paper that opened the modern RL era.

name: VRARA London
bioShort: London chapter of the VR/AR Association; bi-monthly meetups, panels and industry case studies. The convening body for the enterprise side of the London scene.

name: Wagstaffs Design
bioShort: Belvedere Road SE1 PropTech VR/AR/3D agency; co-founder of VU.CITY, the immersive 3D model of London used by planners, developers and the GLA.

name: Walk the Plank
bioShort: Salford-based outdoor arts company that produces Manchester Day Parade and much of the city's fire-and-spectacle work; their commissioned documentation is the richest archive of Manchester fire performance imagery.

name: Warren Clark
bioShort: Corby, Northamptonshire art director on multiplayer-action-RPG mobile games and a prolific print-and-Instagram pixel painter; runs guess-the-film pixel studies.

name: Wim Vanderbauwhede
bioShort: Professor of Computing Science at Glasgow; co-author of High-Performance Computing Using FPGAs (Springer); built a single-FPGA processor carrying more than a thousand cores.

name: William Steptoe
bioShort: UCL Computer Science (VR/AR research); avatars, embodiment, presence; the Beaming project on telepresence. Also worked at Facebook / Reality Labs.

name: Xsens (Movella)
bioShort: High-end inertial suit; Xsens Link is the flagship used by larger UK studios for on-location work where an optical volume cannot be built. Streams into Unreal, Unity and MotionBuilder live.

name: Yarin Gal
bioShort: Group leader of OATML; Tutor in CS at Christ Church; Turing AI Fellow; Research Director at the UK AI Security Institute. OATML's Nature paper on detecting LLM hallucination is one of the most cited 2024 results.

name: Sir Hossein Yassaie
bioShort: CEO of Imagination Technologies 1998–2016; built the licensing business that put PowerVR into the original iPhone and every Apple SoC up to the A10. Knighted 2013.

name: YORD
bioShort: XR & AI creative studio with a London office (HQ in Prague), founded 2019 by Adam and David. Clients include Apple, Meta, LEGO, Bentley.

name: Zestlight Photography
bioShort: Northumbria / North East light-painting workshops covering doodling, light trails and wire wool.

name: Zhi Kang Chua
bioShort: Beltane Fire Society credited photographer; Calton Hill imagery carried in the festival's own galleries and press coverage.

name: Zoubin Ghahramani
bioShort: British-Iranian Fellow of St John's, Cambridge since 2009; VP of Research at Google DeepMind and Professor of Information Engineering at Cambridge. Chief Scientist of Uber 2016–2020. FRS.

name: Zubr
bioShort: Bristol AR/VR studio founded 2015 with the longest production track record — over 400 shipped projects. Operates Curio for museums/heritage work.
